description:
Sites (all in crate-jmap-chat-server/src/):
- chat.rs:406 CHAT_READONLY
- message.rs:514-522 MESSAGE_READONLY
- space.rs:898-906 SPACE_READONLY
- ban.rs:220 BAN_READONLY
- emoji.rs:437 EMOJI_READONLY
- position.rs:208 POSITION_READONLY
- contact.rs:156 CONTACT_READONLY
- presence.rs:161 PRESENCE_READONLY

Each handler defines a hand-keyed list of wire field names that clients MUST NOT patch. Each list has the same shape and is checked the same way:
    let bad_props: Vec<&str> = LIST.iter().copied().filter(|f| patch_val.get(f).is_some()).collect();
    if !bad_props.is_empty() { not_updated.insert(id_str, json!({...})); continue; }

Three problems:
(1) String-keyed: a typo in the constant silently disables protection on that field. There's no spell-check.
(2) Drift: as documented in JMAP-x2gd.14, future additions to jmap-chat-types data structs aren't tracked here. Eight type silos to remember.
(3) Six pages of identical boilerplate that obscures the actually-interesting validation logic for each type (e.g. message.rs's reactions/burn-on-read handling is buried among the boilerplate).

Suggested rewrite: extend the JmapObject (or SetObject) trait to include a const READONLY_FIELDS: &'static [&'static str], and provide a single helper:
    fn reject_readonly_patch<T: SetObject>(patch_val: &Value) -> Result<(), Vec<&'static str>>
…that handlers call uniformly. The const is co-located with the type definition in jmap-chat-types, eliminating drift across crates.

This is an elegance/maintenance refactor, not a correctness fix; the current shape works, it just has surface area that grows with every type added.
title: Eight Space/Message/Chat readonly lists are duplicate boilerplate; consider extracting a trait-derived field set
